title: Environment Variables: make the UI library a control

proposed_comments.title: Clarify the policy loading guarantee (1/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Clarify the policy hosting contract

**Severity:** `low`

The policy property documents that nothing is written, but the guard is in LoadEnvironmentVariables; mutation methods do not use that guard. Please describe the loading/UI behavior instead of promising enforcement for programmatic writes. See the corresponding hosting-guide clarification.

```suggestion
        /// Gets a value indicating whether Group Policy disables the editor. When set, loading is skipped and the page hides its editing controls.
```

confidence.rationale: Exact source has a load guard and public page commands; the proposed change corrects only the documented guarantee, not a claimed reproduced policy bypass.

proposed_comments.title: Clarify host responsibility for programmatic commands (2/2)
proposed_comments.body:
### Clarify the policy hosting contract

**Severity:** `low`

The hosting guide promises that policy disables every write, while the implementation skips loading and hides the editing controls. Public page commands can still be invoked programmatically, so hosts should be told to honor the policy state on those paths. This clarifies the supported hosting contract without changing policy behavior; please also update the IsDisabledByPolicy XML summary.

```suggestion
- **Group Policy**: the library reads `ConfigureEnabledUtilityEnvironmentVariables`, falling back to `ConfigureGlobalUtilityEnabledState`. When disabled, loading is skipped and the page shows an error with its editing controls hidden. Hosts must also honor this state when invoking page commands programmatically. `EnvironmentVariablesPolicy.IsDisabled()` lets a host hide its entry point.
```

confidence.rationale: Exact source has a load guard and public page commands; the proposed change corrects only the documented guarantee, not a claimed reproduced policy bypass.
